content.text:
The in-place, stable comparison sorting algorithm with a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n) and a best-case time complexity of O(n) is **Timsort**.

Timsort is a hybrid sorting algorithm derived from merge sort and insertion sort. It is designed to perform well on many kinds of real-world data, especially data that is partially ordered. Timsort is stable (preserves the relative order of equal elements), in-place (uses O(1) extra space apart from the input array), and has a worst-case time complexity of O(n log n). Its best-case time complexity is O(n) when the input is already sorted or nearly sorted, as it leverages runs of already-sorted elements.

Timsort is the default sorting algorithm in Python's `sorted()` function and `list.sort()`, as well as in Java's `Arrays.sort()` for objects.
